problem.text: Triangle $AMC$ is isosceles with $AM = AC$. Medians $\overline{MV}$ and $\overline{CU}$ are perpendicular to each other, and $MV = CU = 12$. What is the area of $\triangle AMC$?

steps.title: Where to start: cut the medians at the centroid
steps.body: The clue is that we know the full lengths of two medians and the angle between them. The medians meet at the centroid $P$, which splits each median in the ratio $2:1$, with the longer part next to the vertex. Knowing all four pieces around $P$ gives us right triangles to work with.

your_turn.answer: $MP = CP = 8$ and $PV = PU = 4$, since $12$ splits into $8$ and $4$.

steps.title: Find the base $MC$
steps.body: The medians are perpendicular, so $\angle MPC = 90^\circ$. Triangle $MPC$ is a right triangle with legs $MP = CP = 8$, and its hypotenuse is the base $MC$ of the big triangle.

steps.title: Find the equal sides
steps.body: Triangle $UPM$ also has a right angle at $P$, with legs $UP = 4$ and $PM = 8$. Because $CU$ is a median, $U$ is the midpoint of $AM$, so $AM = 2\cdot UM$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
Drop the altitude from $A$ to $MC$. In an isosceles triangle it lands at the midpoint of the base, so the height is $\sqrt{(8\sqrt{5})^2 - (4\sqrt{2})^2} = \sqrt{320 - 32} = \sqrt{288} = 12\sqrt{2}$.
$$[AMC] = \tfrac{1}{2}\cdot 8\sqrt{2}\cdot 12\sqrt{2} = 96$$
The answer is **(C)**.

wrong_choices.B: $\tfrac{1}{2}\cdot 12\cdot 12 = 72$ is the area of quadrilateral $MCVU$, whose diagonals are the two perpendicular medians. That quadrilateral is only part of triangle $AMC$; the top triangle $AUV$ is missing.
